hook.line: Mariana asks Tomás what the people in La Candelaria are like. He can't speak for all of them, but he can say what is usually true.
hook.es: En general, la gente del barrio es muy amable.
hook.en: In general, people in the neighbourhood are very friendly.

examples.es: En general, la gente del barrio es muy amable.
examples.en: In general, people in the neighbourhood are very friendly.

examples.es: Por lo general llego a las ocho.
examples.en: I usually get in at eight.

examples.es: Por norma general, no trabajo los domingos.
examples.en: As a rule, I don't work on Sundays.

examples.en: In general, the café opens at seven.

examples.es: Por lo general, don Hernando toma tinto por la mañana.
examples.en: Don Hernando usually has black coffee in the morning.
What are people like, in general?

rule:
These phrases open a statement about the usual case, not one particular day: *en general*, *por lo general*, *por norma general*.

They can sit at the start, followed by a comma, or at the end of the sentence.

Notice *por lo general*: Spanish needs the *lo*. *Por general* does not exist.

Use them for how things normally are. For one event, say what happened and leave the phrase out: *Ayer cerré a las seis.*
smallPrint: Teachers call these generalising adverbial phrases. *Generalmente* works too, but these three sound more natural in speech.

readAndPick.es: En general, el café abre a las siete.
options: The café opens at seven today.
The café usually opens at seven.

readAndPick.es: Por lo general llego a las ocho.
options: I usually get in at eight.
I got in at eight today.

readAndPick.es: Por norma general, no trabajo los domingos.
options: As a rule, I don't work on Sundays.
What are people like, in general?
What is the person like today?

readAndPick.es: Por lo general, don Hernando toma tinto por la mañana.
options: Don Hernando had black coffee this morning.
Don Hernando usually has black coffee in the morning.

readAndPick.es: En general, la gente del barrio es muy amable.
options: People in the neighbourhood are very friendly in general.

readAndPick.es: Por lo general, cerramos a las seis.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *lo* or *la* and type the whole sentence: *Por ___ general llego a las ocho.*
yourTurn.answer: Por lo general llego a las ocho.
accept: Por lo general, llego a las ocho.
yourTurn.why: The set phrase is *por lo general*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: In general, the café opens at seven.
yourTurn.answer: En general, el café abre a las siete.
accept: En general el café abre a las siete.
El café abre a las siete, en general.
yourTurn.why: *En general* opens a statement about the usual case.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I usually get in at eight.
yourTurn.answer: Por lo general llego a las ocho.
accept: Por lo general, llego a las ocho.
En general llego a las ocho.
En general, llego a las ocho.
yourTurn.why: Usually becomes *por lo general* or *en general*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: As a rule, I don't work on Sundays.
yourTurn.answer: Por norma general, no trabajo los domingos.
accept: Por norma general no trabajo los domingos.
yourTurn.why: *Por norma general* is the "as a rule" version.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: In general, people in the neighbourhood are very friendly.
yourTurn.answer: En general, la gente del barrio es muy amable.
accept: En general la gente del barrio es muy amable.
yourTurn.why: The phrase leads, then the usual case follows.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Yesterday I closed at six. (one day, so no *en general*)
yourTurn.why: One event is a plain statement, with no generalising phrase.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Don Hernando usually has black coffee in the morning.
yourTurn.answer: Por lo general, don Hernando toma tinto por la mañana.
accept: Por lo general don Hernando toma tinto por la mañana.
En general, don Hernando toma tinto por la mañana.
En general don Hernando toma tinto por la mañana.
yourTurn.why: Usually is a job for *por lo general* or *en general*.

pitfalls.wrong: Por general llego a las ocho.
pitfalls.right: Por lo general llego a las ocho.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase needs its *lo*: *por lo general*.

pitfalls.wrong: Ayer, en general, cerré a las seis.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *En general* describes the usual case, not one particular day.

pitfalls.wrong: La gente del barrio son muy amables.
pitfalls.right: La gente del barrio es muy amable.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says people *are*, but *la gente* is singular in Spanish: *es amable*.

personal: Tell us one thing that is usually true about your city or your week, starting with *En general* or *Por lo general*.
